findings.title: Attacks 1 and 10, retest of P5-RT-06-01: the no-JS runs accept a blank T13 panel figure (M9 b3 shadow picture, b7 and b12 restricted board) and a blank T14 board drawing as the default figure
findings.location: site/tests/e2e/nojs.spec.ts:75-180 (toolReport/figureProblems: the first data-board-group is the figure; any role=img element with a child element counts as a drawing); site/tests/e2e/M9.spec.ts:278-343 ('M9 renders without JavaScript'); site/tests/e2e/T14.spec.ts:138-147 and :822
findings.claim: The P5 fix taught nojs.spec.ts the parts of T12's figure only. A blank T13 panel figure and a blank T14 board drawing are still accepted as the default figure, because the predicate checks a figure's container and not its marks.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.4: 'A Playwright run with JavaScript disabled checks, for every lesson, that the text, every default figure and every table are present'; SPEC 4 T13 'Shadows: ... a picture' and 'Restricted board: drawn in Bourbaki order'; SPEC 4 T14's board drawing. A root whose configured figure has no marks should be rejected.
findings.observed: With JS off on modules/m9-real-forms/, the reproducer removes every element inside b3's shadow-picture SVG (4 point circles before) and the drawing and node buttons of b7's and b12's restricted board. The current predicate still accepts the roots: ['b3 as board', 'b7 as board', 'b12 as board'], and M9.spec.ts's per-instance checks still pass. On atlas/B3/ and tools/atlas/, removing every line, path, circle, polygon and text from the role=img drawings (empty g groups kept) leaves the root accepted ('atlas (page) as drawing'), and T14.spec.ts's checks (drawing visible, aria-label set) still pass.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/redteam-RT-06-p6-playwright.config.ts site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-06-p6-nojs-blank-figure.spec.ts (the config starts astro preview on RT06_PORT, default 5560; under heavy load start it first with node node_modules/astro/bin/astro.mjs preview --root site --port 5560 --ignore-lock). 3 tests fail with the arrays above.
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 7.4 'Without JavaScript' (last sentence); 4 T13 Shadows and Restricted board; 4 T14; 7.7 row 'Without JavaScript'; RED-TEAM-COMMON 2 ('a test that would pass against an empty function'); retest of P5-RT-06-01
findings.proposedFix: Make the figure check content-based for every figure: a role=img drawing, a data-out figure SVG or a board must hold at least one mark (circle, line, path, polygon or text outside title and desc). Have nojs.spec.ts read the figure of the panel each T13 instance is configured to show (data-out shadow-picture, restricted-board), and have M9.spec.ts check b3's points and b7/b12's restricted nodes.

findings.title: Attack 29: restrictedBoard's board comes back from the worker as the canonical F4 (another position order and matrix) on E8 e8(-24), because workerWire sends a named board by its name alone
findings.location: site/src/lib/workerWire.ts:62-64 (specOf: name whenever board.name is set) and the Board branch of serialize (:86-92); packages/engine/src/satake.ts:431-443 (the restricted board is named after identify() but keeps the orbit order, labels 4,3,2,1)
findings.claim: On the E-9 worker path that phase 6 added for E7 and E8, restrictedBoard's board field does not match the main-thread result: the positions are in another order, with another matrix in position order.
findings.expected: CONTRACTS 4: 'Board as its BoardSpec (rebuilt with resolveBoard)', and RestrictedBoard { ...; board: Board } (CONTRACTS 2). Attack 29: the worker path computes the same thing as the main thread, so the board must not come back 'with another matrix'.
findings.observed: For e8(-24) (black 2,3,4,5), the direct call gives board.name 'F4' with cartan rows [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-2,0],[0,-1,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]] and labels [4,3,2,1]. Through engine.worker.ts's handleCall, the same call returns cartan [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-1,0],[0,-2,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]] and labels [1,2,3,4]. The other fields (orbits, simpleRestrictedRoots2, cartan, compositeWords) stay in the direct board's position order, so mapping an orbit to its label through rb.board gives a different label on the worker path. satake and matchCatalogue round-trip exactly for all 8 E7/E8 records. No visible effect today: T13 never reads rb.board (t13/model.ts:387 says the worker rebuilds it by name).
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline; node_modules/.bin/vitest run site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-06-p6-worker-satake.test.ts -t "restricted board that comes back" (needs no build; if Vite's SSR cache is stale, set TMPDIR to a fresh directory). 1 test fails with the diff above. The same file's 'E8 e8(-24): satake, restrictedBoard and matchCatalogue equal the direct call' fails on the same field.
findings.specRef: CONTRACTS.md 4 (worker.ts serialisation) and 2 (RestrictedBoard.board); SPEC.md 5.1 E-9 rule 3 (restrictedBoard for E7 and E8 runs in the worker); RT-06 attack 29
findings.proposedFix: In specOf, send { cartan } (with the labels, or a flag) unless the board's matrix and labels equal those of resolveBoard(name). Or have the engine name a restricted board only when its positions are in Bourbaki order, or build it in Bourbaki order.
